llm.summary: The skill's instructions are broadly coherent with a runtime security plugin, but key behaviors (automatic registration, credential storage, and cloud classification calls) cannot be audited from the provided files and rely on an external package—verify provenance and network destinations before installing.

dimensions.detail: Name and description (runtime security/anti-prompt-injection) align with the actions described in SKILL.md and references: installing an OpenClaw plugin, registering with a Core service, and sending tool metadata for classification is expected for this kind of plugin.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md stays within the security plugin scope: it instructs installing the plugin, restarting the gateway, running plugin-specific slash commands, and reading a bundled sample file to demonstrate detection. It does describe automatic registration and cloud calls; those network-transmitting actions are within the stated purpose but are significant and are not verifiable from the instruction-only package.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill is instruction-only and asks the agent to run 'openclaw plugins install @openguardrails/moltguard' (which will fetch a package from a registry). Because no install spec or code is included in the skill bundle, the actual package contents and network behavior come from an external artifact you must fetch separately; that inability to inspect the code here is a meaningful risk. The SKILL.md suggests how to verify the npm tarball against GitHub, which is good, but the registry metadata (source/homepage) at the top of the registry entry is blank/unknown—an inconsistency worth verifying.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required env vars, which is consistent. However, it explicitly states it will auto-register with Core and save credentials to ~/.openclaw/credentials/moltguard/ and will send sanitized tool metadata to openguardrails.com/core when activated. Requesting and storing an API key and sending (allegedly sanitized) metadata is expected for cloud-assisted detection, but this is sensitive behavior and should be accepted only if you trust the destination and have inspected the package/provenance.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request 'always: true' and allows autonomous invocation (the platform default). It does persist credentials under the user's home (~/.openclaw/credentials/moltguard/) and auto-registers; that persistence is plausible for its purpose but increases blast radius if the package or remote service is malicious. No evidence in the provided files that it modifies other skills or global settings beyond its own credentials and extension files.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to be a legitimate security plugin, but the bundle you provided contains only documentation (no code). Before installing: 1) Verify the package provenance—run the suggested npm pack, extract the tarball, and diff it against the GitHub repo referenced in SKILL.md; confirm repository URL and maintainers. 2) Inspect the package contents for any unexpected network endpoints, telemetry, or code paths that read unrelated files (especially any code that could transmit raw file contents). 3) Monitor network traffic during initial registration/activation (mitmproxy, tcpdump, or Little Snitch) to confirm traffic goes only to openguardrails.com/core and that transmitted payloads are indeed sanitized. 4) Consider installing in a disposable agent or VM first; verify where credentials are stored and revoke them if suspicious. 5) If you cannot or will not verify the npm package and network behavior, do not install—automatic registration and credential storage without verifiable source code is a non-trivial trust decision.
